quick.summary: Why beautiful work gets cut, and how to make sure yours matters.
quick.takeaway: Focus your design effort on the main goal of the business.

beats.line: I spent a week polishing an animation. Then the manager cut it. Why?
You painted the kitchen instead of the dining room.
Wait. I do not have a kitchen.
Think of a restaurant. Decorating the kitchen only pleases the chefs.
Customers never see it. The owner gains nothing from it.
Your animation was beautiful. But it ignored the main business goal.
Can I just say picking the right battle?
Yes. You must serve both the customer and the business.
So I should check the main goal before I obsess over details.
Exactly. That keeps your work off the cutting room floor.

quiz.question: Before starting a new feature, what is the best thing to ask?
options: What is the main business goal?
How many animations can we fit?
Can we use a new font?
quiz.explanation: Knowing the goal ensures your work is valuable to both the user and the company.

quiz.question: A good design always gets built, even if it ignores business goals.
quiz.explanation: If it does not help the business, it will likely be cut.
